12.1.b:
MUST-KNOW — 60-second answer: "how do you read alignment on a TKA film?"
- "**Knee Society** system → AP + lateral · four angles: α, β on AP · γ, δ on lateral."
- "Targets → femur 5–7° valgus to its shaft · tibia **90°** to its axis → neutral mechanical axis."
- "Judge on a **standing long-leg film**, limb not rotated → patella forward."

### Knee Society angles
- **Knee Society** radiographic evaluation (1989) → standard AP + lateral for any TKA (Campbell)
[[FIG: Fig 12.1 · 12.1
- Few use the whole form → most check only **notching** (Prof Sherief Khaled)

| Angle | View | Measures | Target |
|---|---|---|---|
| **α** | AP | femoral component vs femoral shaft | 90° − valgus cut → 5° cut = 85° |
| **β** | AP | tibial component vs tibial shaft | 90° |
| **Ω** | AP | total valgus (femur + tibia) | neutral mechanical axis |
| **γ** | lateral | femoral component flexion | near neutral |
| **δ** | lateral | tibial component vs tibial shaft (= slope) | by design (12.3) |

- Lecturer's names → α = distal femoral angle, β = proximal tibial angle
- Film version of the cuts → wrong angle = wrong cut · cut technique → chapter 10

### Axes behind the numbers
- Native knee → tibial surface **3° varus**, femoral surface 9° valgus to the **anatomical** axis (Campbell)
- Femoral anatomical axis → 6° from mechanical, 9° from vertical → angles **81° and 99°** (Prof Sherief Khaled)
[[FIG: Fig 12.2 · 12.1
- Tibia → mechanical = anatomical axis · 1–2° difference ignored
- Femoral component → **5–7° valgus** · tibial component → perpendicular to tibial mechanical axis (Campbell)

#### Why it matters
- Native anatomical LDFA (lateral distal femoral angle) 81° · after TKA 83–85° · MPTA (medial proximal tibial angle) 90°

### Reading the film correctly
- Alignment judged on a **standing long-leg film** · short films mislead → rotation, limited shafts
[[FIG: Fig 12.3 · 12.1
- **Limb rotation** alters coronal angles → patella facing forward, normal fibular overlap

PITFALL — the rotated AP
- External or internal limb rotation fakes varus or valgus on a short knee film
- Say → "**I measure on a standing long-leg film with the patella forward and normal fibular overlap**"

HIGH YIELD — Memory line
- **α 85 · β 90 · femur 5–7 valgus · tibia never >5 varus · long leg, patella forward**

12.2.t: Component Positioning — Lateral View, Fit & Rotation
12.2.b:
MUST-KNOW — 60-second answer: "what do you check on the lateral and for fit?"
- "Lateral → femoral flexion (γ), **anterior notching**, posterior condylar offset restored."
- "Fit → tibia flush with cortex · no overhang · central, not eccentric placement."
- "Rotation is invisible on plain films → **CT** in the painful TKA."

### Femoral component on the lateral
- Too much **extension** → **anterior notching** → fracture risk · too much flexion → limits extension
- γ (lecturer: theta angle) → femoral component aligned with the femoral shaft (Prof Sherief Khaled)
- Anatomical axis → two point pairs ≈10 cm apart, bisected → implant perpendicular to it (Prof Abd Elkarim)
[[FIG: Fig 12.4 · 12.2

#### Posterior condylar offset
- Offset → posterior femoral cortex tangent to posterior condylar cortex → compare pre- vs postoperative (Prof Abd Elkarim)
[[FIG: Fig 12.5 · 12.2
- Alternative → ratio from the **anterior femoral cortex** → should be unchanged
- Poor film → ask for a **true lateral** → posterior osteophytes gone, offset kept → full flexion
[[FIG: Fig 12.6 · 12.2

### Component fit & overhang
- Tibia **flush with cortex** → undersized sinks into cancellous bone · oversized impinges
[[FIG: Fig 12.7 · 12.2
- Overhang = metal on tendon or ligament → localised pain, not instability
- ML (mediolateral) femoral overhang → collateral irritation → persistent pain

| Overhang | Structure irritated |
|---|---|
| **Coronal** | collateral ligaments |
| **Anterior** | patellar tendon |
| **Posterior** | popliteal structures |

### Placement, coverage & rotation
- **Eccentric placement** (medial/lateral, superior/inferior) → subluxation, dislocation (Prof Sherief Khaled)
- **Tibial surface coverage** → % of cut surface covered → Knee Society item
- Bilateral case → right tibia fits, left overhangs → case for **gender-specific** implants or PSI (patient-specific instruments)
[[FIG: Fig 12.8 · 12.2
- **Rotation** → not seen on plain films → **CT**

#### CT rotation targets
- Femur → posterior condylar axis parallel or slightly externally rotated to the **epicondylar axis** (Miller)
- Tibia → tray axis over the **medial third of the tibial tubercle** (Miller)
- Femoral internal rotation → flexion-gap imbalance, lateral patellar tilt → see chapter 13

PITFALL — pain with a "perfect" film
- Plain films cannot show component rotation → internal rotation is a classic hidden cause
- Say → "**painful TKA with normal films → CT for femoral and tibial rotation**"

HIGH YIELD — Memory line
- **Lateral: no notch, offset kept · flush, no overhang · rotation = CT, tray over medial third of tubercle**

12.3.b:
MUST-KNOW — 60-second answer: "how do you measure tibial slope on the film?"
- "Line along the **anterior tibial cortex** → perpendicular → angle to the articular line."
- "Native average **7–10°** · target set by design → PS cut at 90°, CR slope per design."
- "Only on a **true lateral** → condyles superimposed · proximal 10–15 cm of tibia is enough."

### What the angle shows
- Slope = perpendicular to the tibial shaft vs upper tibial surface = Knee Society **δ**
- Gap logic → chapter 11

### How to measure it
- **JAAOS method** → line A on anterior cortex · B perpendicular · slope = B vs articular line (Prof Abd Elkarim)
[[FIG: Fig 12.9 · 12.3
- Articular line → through 3–4 prominent points, **anterior tibial corner** included
- Typical 5°, 7° or 10° · average **7–10°**
- Long-leg lateral not needed → **proximal 10–15 cm** of tibia suffices

### Target by design & guide
- Posterior tilt of the tibial component → depends on articular design (Campbell)
- Slope by design → 10 Technique
- Advanced extramedullary guide → e.g. 89° · CR tolerates more slope than PS

#### Guide accuracy (cadaver)
- **Anterior tibial crest** reference → 3.2° varus to 2.1° valgus, consistent anterior slope (Campbell)
- **Intramedullary** guide → less accurate than extramedullary for posterior slope

#### Which condyle is which
- **Medial condyle** → longer articular surface · projects slightly **lower** (more distal) (Campbell)
- **Lateral condyle** → wider · carries the **sulcus terminalis** notch (Campbell, Miller)
- Rotated film → name each outline first, then judge slope

PITFALL — the rotated lateral
- Condyles not superimposed → slope and femoral flexion both unreliable
- Say → "**I measure slope only on a true lateral with the condyles superimposed**"

HIGH YIELD — Memory line
- **Anterior cortex → perpendicular → articular line · native 7–10° · PS 90°, CR per design · true lateral only**

12.4.b:
MUST-KNOW — 60-second answer: "how do you call a TKA loose on X-ray?"
- "Zones → tibia **7** AP + 3 lateral · femur **7** lateral · patella 5 · sum lucency depth (mm)."
- "Cemented → **complete line ≥2 mm** = loose · incomplete <2 mm common, harmless."
- "Other signs → progression, **migration**, subsidence · exclude **infection** first."

### Knee Society zones
- Zones → common wording, serial comparison · developers superimpose their silhouette on the form (Campbell)
[[FIG: Fig 12.10 · 12.4

| Component (view) | Zones | Layout |
|---|---|---|
| **Tibia (AP)** | 7 | 1–2 medial plateau · 3–4 lateral · 5–7 medial stem, tip, lateral stem |
| **Tibia (lateral)** | 3 | 1 anterior · 2 posterior · 3 stem tip |
| **Femur (lateral)** | 7 | 1–2 anterior flange · 3–4 posterior condyle · 5–7 chamfers and peg |
| **Patella (axial)** | 5 | 1–2 edges · 3–5 around pegs (3 if one peg) |

- Each zone → lucency depth in mm → summed per component (Campbell)

### Reading lucent lines
| Score (seven-zone tibia) | Meaning |
|---|---|
| **≤4**, non-progressive | probably insignificant |
| **5–9** | close follow-up for progression |
| **≥10** | possible or impending failure, even without symptoms |

- Thresholds → Campbell and Prof Sherief Khaled agree
- Stable thin line common · **widening** or spread on serial films → loosening

#### Loosening signs
- Cemented → complete line **≥2 mm** at bone–cement interface → aseptic loosening (Campbell)
[[FIG: Fig 12.11 · 12.4
- Incomplete line **<2 mm** → common, no link with poor outcome
- Uncemented → lines = no ingrowth · extensive, progressive or painful → consider loosening
- **Migration** or subsidence on sequential films · stem tilt with periosteal reaction (Miller)

#### Infection first
- Progressive lucency + pain → exclude **infection** first → CRP, ESR, aspiration → chapter 6

### When the standard film is not enough
- Line under a metal-backed tray → hidden by **4°** of knee flexion → identical views each visit (Campbell)
- **Fluoroscopy** → beam parallel to implant surfaces → hidden lucencies in unexplained pain
- **CT with 3D reconstruction** → loosening, defect size, fracture extent despite artefact (Prof Abd Elkarim)

PITFALL — lucency is not always aseptic
- A progressive line in a painful knee may be infection, not wear or loosening
- Say → "**progressive lucency + pain → CRP, ESR, aspiration before calling it aseptic**"

HIGH YIELD — Memory line
- **7–3–7–5 zones · 4 / 5–9 / 10 · complete 2 mm = loose · 4° flexion hides it · infection first**

12.5.b:
MUST-KNOW — 60-second answer: "what do you check for the patella after TKA?"
- "Lateral → **height** (Insall–Salvati, Blackburne–Peel), fracture · joint line not raised."
- "**Merchant** (skyline) → tilt, subluxation, button position → lateral tilt = **maltracking**."
- "Maltracking → think **component rotation** → CT."

### Views & problem list
- **Lateral + Merchant** (skyline) → medialisation or lateralisation, tracking, tilt, button position
- **Skyline view** → patella and its tracking (Prof Shokry)
- Knee Society **patellar problem list** → angle, placement, subluxation, dislocation (Campbell)
- Case → button centred, rotation correct, slightly **medial** · lateral button → trouble
[[FIG: Fig 12.12 · 12.5

### Joint line height
- Joint-line landmarks and the 4 mm limit → 10 Technique

### Patellar height
- **Insall–Salvati** → patellar tendon ÷ longest patellar length · normal 1.0 · <0.8 baja, >1.2 alta (Miller)
[[FIG: Fig 12.13 · 12.5
- **Blackburne–Peel** → plateau line to articular lower edge ÷ articular length · normal 0.54–1.06 (Campbell)
- Insall–Salvati ignores the tibia → unchanged by a raised joint line
- Blackburne–Peel uses the plateau → falls when the joint line rises

### Tilt & subluxation
- Merchant tilt or lateral subluxation → **maltracking** → check component rotation
[[FIG: Fig 12.14 · 12.5
- Maltracking, baja and patellar fracture → chapters 13–14

PITFALL — normal Insall–Salvati, low patella
- Joint-line elevation lowers the patella relative to the joint, but Insall–Salvati stays normal
- Say → "**after TKA I use Blackburne–Peel and the joint-line landmarks, not Insall–Salvati alone**"

HIGH YIELD — Memory line
- **Joint line within 4 mm · IS 0.8–1.2 · Blackburne–Peel after TKA · tilt on Merchant = rotation**
